chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Norman Granz brings Charlie Parker to record with the band
summary: Granz, linked to Chico O'Farrill, heard the band at Birdland and the Palladium and wanted Parker to record "El Manicero".

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Okay, with Mercury, that's when things started happening with Charlie Parker and Flip Phillips.

Now,you did some nice Mercury recordings, you know, "Hall of the Mambo King", "At Sunrise" and that. How soon later or who approached you with the idea of bringing the Machito orchestra together with Charlie Parker?
Okay. Do you remember what happened or how it came about?
Norman Granz was connected with Chico O'Farrill because Chico O'Farrill already had name as an arranger, because he did a lot, a lot ......
He did "Carambola" for Kenton and Dizzy Gillespie.

Yeah, and Dizzy Gillespie and to Benny Goodman, those guys; so he had a reputation already. So one day Mario Bauza and Charlie Parker and Norman Granz we got together because we was working a the Birdland and that particular week Norman Granz came to New York and hit the Birdland and he flipped, he liked what he ..., so from Birdland we went to the Palladium, so he took Charlie Parker to listen to the band to see if he liked to record with us. So he liked.

As a matter of fact, he had in mind to record "El Manicero". "El Manicero", to many people, even to Cubans or to Spanish people, is a number that is easy and is pleasant. Is not too complicated, is a very flowing melody. But it had some kind of trick in the phrase. You just can't play tata ta ta tata, because sound corny and you just can't --- In those days, now is better, take the way of the expression of the American,

black-American, musicians to bring from jazz to Latin music, to play a Latin melody with all his roots in his music that is definite, is well created and well complete. So is like a person move from Miami to Alaska.
